AdminBackupRequest.description:
AdminBackupRequest is the body of POST /api/admin/backup (optional): the
file name of the backup in the backup directory (letters, digits, ".",
"_" and "-"; default ai-observer-backup-<time>.duckdb)

AdminBackupResponse.description: AdminBackupResponse describes a backup: a DuckDB database file

AdminDatabaseSize.description:
AdminDatabaseSize is the space the database takes: the file and its
write-ahead log, and the used and free blocks inside the file

compactRecommended.description:
CompactRecommended is set when so much of the file is free that
ai-observer compact (with the server stopped) would shrink it
noticeably

AdminDeleteRequest.description:
AdminDeleteRequest is the body of POST /api/admin/delete: the telemetry
in [from, to] (RFC 3339, both required) of a service filter (a tool name
such as codex selects all of its services, a service name only itself;
empty for all) and a scope (logs, metrics, traces or all, the default).
DryRun only counts the records.

AdminDeleteResponse.description:
AdminDeleteResponse counts the records deleted, or those a dry run would
delete (traces only then). Database is the space of the database after
the deletion and a checkpoint; the file keeps its size.

AdminExportRequest.description:
AdminExportRequest is the body of POST /api/admin/export (optional): the
directory name of the export in the backup directory (letters, digits,
".", "_" and "-"; default ai-observer-export-<source>-<time>), the source
(a tool name or all, the default), an optional range and whether to
write a ZIP archive

AdminExportResponse.description:
AdminExportResponse describes an export: its directory, the files in it
and the rows exported

BatchMetricSeriesRequest.description: BatchMetricSeriesRequest represents a batch query for multiple metric series

timeZone.description: TimeZone is the IANA zone buckets are aligned to (default UTC)

BatchMetricSeriesResponse.description: BatchMetricSeriesResponse contains results for all queried metrics

BreakdownValuesResponse.description: BreakdownValuesResponse lists the values of a metric's attribute

CreateDashboardRequest.description: CreateDashboardRequest is the body of POST /api/dashboards

CreateHTTPCaptureRunRequest.description:
CreateHTTPCaptureRunRequest starts a launcher run (ai-observer run): the
server opens a proxy port for it alone

CreateWidgetRequest.description: CreateWidgetRequest is the body of POST /api/dashboards/{id}/widgets

DashboardWidget.description: DashboardWidget represents a widget placed on a dashboard

DashboardWithWidgets.description: DashboardWithWidgets represents a full dashboard with its widgets

DeleteScope.description: What a deletion deletes: logs, metrics, traces or all of them

ErrorResponse.description: ErrorResponse is the body of error responses (status 4xx and 5xx)

error.description: Error is the HTTP status text, such as "Bad Request"

message.description: Message says what went wrong (for server errors without internals)

HTTPBodyPart.description: Body parts and their file names

HTTPBodyVariant.description:
Body variants an exchange stores (HTTPExchangeBody.Variant)
- safe: redacted copy
- raw: as observed, local and sensitive (full_raw)
- none: not stored (metadata_only, or nothing observed)

HTTPCaptureMode.description:
What the capture stores: safe (redacted bodies), metadata_only (no bodies) or full_raw (also unredacted bodies, local files)
- safe: CaptureSafe stores bodies with secrets redacted (default)
- metadata_only: CaptureMetadataOnly stores no bodies, only metadata (status, timing, model, usage, sizes, hashes)
- full_raw: CaptureFullRaw also stores the bodies as observed, unredacted, in local files (explicit opt-in for controlled classroom use)

HTTPCaptureRun.description:
HTTPCaptureRun is a capture run: the exchanges of one launched process,
or of the shared manual port during one server start

cwd.description: Cwd, Command and PID of a launched process

exchanges.description: Exchanges observed, and the last one's time

sessionIds.description:
SessionIDs are the Claude Code session IDs the exchanges carried
(X-Claude-Code-Session-Id or metadata.user_id)

unattributed.description: Unattributed counts exchanges without a session ID

HTTPCaptureRunCreated.description: HTTPCaptureRunCreated is the started run and its proxy URL

HTTPCaptureRunMode.description: How a capture run records: manual (the shared proxy port) or launcher (ai-observer run, a port of its own)

HTTPCaptureRunsResponse.description: HTTPCaptureRunsResponse is a page of capture runs, newest first

HTTPCostComponent.description: HTTPCostComponent is one priced part of an exchange's usage

component.description:
Component: input, output, cache_read, cache_write_5m, cache_write_1h,
cache_write_unknown

pricePerMTok.description: PricePerMTok is the catalog price per million tokens; nil: no price

HTTPExchange.description: HTTPExchange is a row of the timeline: one request and its response

degraded.description:
Degraded: part of this exchange was not captured (traffic was not
affected)

durationMs.description: Durations from the start in milliseconds (nil: not reached)

headline.description: Headline is a one-sentence, evidence-based description

requestBytes.description: Body sizes as observed on the wire

requestId.description: RequestID is the upstream's request-id response header

retryCount.description: RetryCount is the client's X-Stainless-Retry-Count header

seq.description: Seq is the exchange's position in its run (1-based, by arrival)

sessionId.description: SessionID and the evidence it came from (header or body field)

status.description: Status is the HTTP status the client received (0: none)

toolUses.description:
ToolUses names the tools the reply requested; ToolResults counts
tool results the request carried for the first time

HTTPExchangeBody.description: HTTPExchangeBody is one side of an exchange: headers and body

bodyEncoding.description: BodyEncoding is utf8 or base64 (bytes that are no valid UTF-8)

contentType.description:
ContentType and ContentEncoding headers; DecodeStatus says how the
body was decoded for display (identity, decoded, unsupported, error)

message.description: Message is the interpreted reply (part response, Messages API)

observedBytes.description:
ObservedBytes and ObservedSHA256 describe the bytes on the wire
(encoded); the SHA-256 is empty when bytes were lost

request.description: Request is the interpreted request (part request, Messages API)

sanitized.description: Sanitized: redaction changed the stored safe variant

storedBytes.description: StoredBytes and StoredSHA256 describe the returned variant (decoded)

truncated.description:
Truncated: the body exceeded the storage limit; only its start is
stored (the traffic was forwarded whole)

unavailable.description: Unavailable explains a missing body (metadata_only, not captured)

variant.description:
Variant of the body returned: safe (redacted), raw (as observed,
full_raw only) or none

HTTPExchangeDetail.description:
HTTPExchangeDetail is an exchange with its transport lifecycle and
interpretation (GET /api/http-inspector/exchanges/{id})

degradedReasons.description: DegradedReasons explain what was not captured

prevId.description: Previous and next exchange of the run, for navigation

HTTPExchangeKind.description:
ExchangeKind is what an observed HTTP exchange was, by its endpoint
- model_inference: KindModelInference is POST /v1/messages: the model generated a reply
- token_count: KindTokenCount is POST /v1/messages/count_tokens: an estimate of the input tokens of a request, no generation
- other_api: KindOtherAPI is any other path that went through the proxy
- transport_error: KindTransportError is an exchange that got no upstream response

HTTPExchangeState.description:
Exchange states: what the proxy observed of an exchange
- partial: ExchangePartial: the response ended without its normal end (stream without message_stop, body read error), or the request body was not read whole
- aborted: ExchangeAborted: the client went away before the response ended
- failed: ExchangeFailed: no upstream response (connection, timeout)
- interrupted: ExchangeInterrupted: the server stopped before the exchange ended

HTTPExchangesResponse.description: HTTPExchangesResponse is a page of exchanges in run order

HTTPHeader.description: HTTPHeader is a header as stored: secret values are never stored

redacted.description: Redacted: the value was replaced (credentials, cookies)

HTTPInspectorStatus.description:
HTTPInspectorStatus describes the HTTP capture proxy (GET
/api/http-inspector/status). It never contains credentials.

degraded.description: Degraded: some capture was lost since the start

enabled.description: Enabled: the proxy runs with this server

host.description: Host and Port of the shared listener (Port 0: none, launcher runs only)

manualRunId.description: ManualRunID is the run of the shared listener

proxyUrl.description:
ProxyURL is the value for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (empty without a shared
listener)

HTTPLifecycleEvent.description: HTTPLifecycleEvent is a transport event of an exchange

event.description:
Event: request_started, request_body_observed, upstream_connected,
response_headers_received, response_streaming, completed,
upstream_error, client_aborted, upstream_aborted, capture_degraded,
stream_parse_error

HTTPRequestDiffResponse.description:
HTTPRequestDiffResponse compares a request with an earlier one of the
same session and kind

comparedBy.description:
ComparedBy says how the previous exchange was chosen:
same_conversation (equal first message), same_model,
previous_in_session, none

previousId.description: PreviousID is the compared exchange (empty: none, everything is new)

HTTPRunDetail.description: HTTPRunDetail is a run with its summary

HTTPSSEEvent.description: HTTPSSEEvent is one Server-Sent Event of a streamed response

data.description:
Data is the event's data (redacted in safe mode, empty in
metadata_only)

event.description: Event is the event: field; Type the JSON "type"

offsetMs.description: OffsetMs is the time since the request started

HTTPSSEEventsResponse.description: HTTPSSEEventsResponse is a page of an exchange's SSE events in order

types.description: Types counts all events of the exchange by type

runs.description: Runs that carried the session's exchanges

HTTPSessionTrafficResponse.description:
HTTPSessionTrafficResponse is the API traffic of a Claude Code session
(GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/http-exchanges)

HTTPSourceComparison.description:
HTTPSourceComparison sets the proxy's usage of a session beside what
OTLP and session files recorded, without adding them up

certainty.description: Certainty: exact (every inference exchange matched), partial, none

matchedRequests.description:
MatchedRequests: exchanges whose request-id also appears in the
session's telemetry (same model request seen by both)

proxyInputTokens.description:
ProxyInputTokens / ProxyOutputTokens: the proxy's final usage
(input = uncached + cache read + cache write)

selected.description:
Selected is the source of the session totals shown elsewhere in AI
Observer (otlp/local_jsonl, unchanged by the proxy)

telemetryInputTokens.description:
Telemetry usage of the session (OTLP or session file, deduplicated
by AI Observer's existing rules); nil when unknown

HTTPTokenTotals.description:
HTTPTokenTotals are summed usage fields; CacheReadShare is cache reads
over total input tokens

HTTPToolLink.description:
HTTPToolLink is a tool use requested by a reply and the request that
carried its result

evidence.description: Evidence names how the link was made

input.description: Input is the tool's arguments (redacted; empty in metadata_only)

resultExchangeId.description:
ResultExchangeID is the first exchange whose request carried the
tool_result with this ID

useExchangeId.description: UseExchangeID is the exchange whose reply requested the tool

HTTPToolLinkStatus.description: Correlation states of a tool use

HTTPToolLinksResponse.description: HTTPToolLinksResponse lists a run's tool uses in order

note.description: Note reminds that local execution is not observed

HTTPTrafficSummary.description: HTTPTrafficSummary aggregates exchanges (a run, or a session)

costUsd.description:
CostUSD is the estimated API-equivalent cost of the priced exchanges;
CostStatus is partial when some were not priced

countedTokens.description: CountedTokens sums count_tokens results (estimates, not usage)

durationMs.description: DurationMs from the first request to the last response

tokens.description:
Tokens of inference exchanges with final usage; PartialTokens of
those with partial usage, kept apart

HTTPUsage.description:
HTTPUsage is the token usage of an exchange: the API's usage object,
normalized (nil: not reported, never 0), with derived totals and the
estimated API-equivalent cost

costUsd.description:
CostUSD is the API-equivalent cost estimated from the price catalog
(not a subscription charge); nil when not estimable

countTokens.description:
CountTokens is the input_tokens of a count_tokens response: an
estimate, not inference usage

pricedModel.description: PricedModel is the catalog model the cost used

quality.description:
Quality: final (complete response), partial (interrupted: the last
cumulative values observed), unavailable (no usage)

source.description: Source is always http_proxy: captured on the wire

snapshots.description: Snapshots are the usage objects of the stream in order (cumulative)

HTTPUsageDetail.description: HTTPUsageDetail is the usage of one exchange with its stream snapshots

HealthResponse.description:
HealthResponse is the answer of GET /health (liveness): always "ok" while
the server answers

HistogramStat.description:
Statistic of a histogram metric's series: avg (the default), sum, count, min, max or a percentile
(estimated from the histogram buckets)

InternalBucket.description:
InternalBucket counts the observations up to LE (cumulative; the last
bucket, LE "+Inf", counts all)

InternalMetric.description: InternalMetric is a metric family: its series by label values

type.description: Type is counter, gauge or histogram

InternalMetricSeries.description:
InternalMetricSeries is one series of a metric. Counters and gauges have
Value; histograms have Count, Sum and cumulative Buckets.

InternalMetricType.description: Type of a metric of AI Observer itself

InternalMetricsResponse.description:
InternalMetricsResponse is the answer of GET /api/internal/metrics: AI
Observer's own metrics (internal/selfmetrics), also served in the
Prometheus text format at GET /metrics

startedAt.description: StartedAt is when the counters started (process start), RFC 3339

LogLevelCounts.description:
LogLevelCounts is the answer of GET /api/logs/levels: the number of log
records per severity text, such as {"INFO": 120, "ERROR": 3} (records
without one are not counted)

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the stored session of the log (read from storage;
ignored when logs are stored, which take it from LogAttributes)

LogsResponse.description: LogsResponse is a page of log records, the newest first

nextCursor.description: NextCursor selects the next page (cursor parameter) when HasMore

MetricAttributeKeysResponse.description: MetricAttributeKeysResponse lists the attribute keys of a metric's points

MetricDataPoint.description:
MetricDataPoint is a metric point. Which value fields are set depends on
MetricType: Value for gauges and sums; Count, Sum, Min, Max and buckets
for histograms; quantiles for summaries.

MetricNamesResponse.description: MetricNamesResponse lists the names of stored metrics

MetricQuery.description: MetricQuery represents a single query within a batch request

filters.description: Filters keep only points whose attributes have these exact values

groupBy.description:
GroupBy names up to two point attributes: series are grouped by
service and their values (labelled by the keys) instead of by type

merge.description:
Merge makes one series of all matching points, without a service
label (for a single value of an average or percentile); it takes no
GroupBy

stat.description:
Stat is the statistic of a histogram metric: avg (default), sum,
count, min, max, p50, p90, p95 or p99

MetricQueryResult.description: MetricQueryResult contains the result for a single metric query

error.description: Error says why a query failed, and Code is its kind (MetricError*)

metricType.description: MetricType and Stat as in TimeSeriesResponse

MetricType.description: Type of metric points, as OTLP names them

MetricsResponse.description: MetricsResponse is a page of metric points, the newest first

nextCursor.description: NextCursor selects the next page (cursor parameter) when HasMore

OKResponse.description:
OKResponse is the answer of requests that return no data, such as
making a dashboard the default or moving widgets: {"status": "ok"}

Provider.description: Provider describes a supported AI coding tool (tools.Provider)

otherServices.description: OtherServices are further service names the tool sends

ProviderService.description: ProviderService is a further service name of a tool (tools.Service)

ReadyResponse.description:
ReadyResponse is the answer of GET /ready (readiness): Status and Database
are "ok" (200) when the database answers a query, else "unavailable"
(503) with Error

RedactionMode.description:
Mode selects what is redacted
- off: Off stores telemetry as it is received
- secrets: Secrets redacts credentials: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys
- all: All redacts secrets and personal data

ServerMode.description:
Server modes reported by GET /api/status
- serve: OTLP and API
- watch: session files and API, no OTLP
- serve+watch: OTLP, session files and API (serve --watch)

ServicesResponse.description: ServicesResponse lists the services that sent telemetry

Session.description: Session represents a conversation session summary

costUsd.description:
Usage summed over the session's logs that become transcript messages
and carry it (tools.CostKeys, InputTokenKeys, OutputTokenKeys); nil
when none does

httpExchanges.description:
HTTPExchanges counts the session's Anthropic API exchanges captured by
the HTTP Inspector's proxy (0: none captured)

repository.description:
Repository and Branch attribute the session to a Git repository (the
latest of its logs that names them: imported and watched sessions)

snippet.description:
Search results only: the text around the terms in the newest matching
record (redacted), the number of matching records in the range, and
the time of the newest

title.description:
Title is the session's first user prompt, on one line, cut to 200
characters and redacted (storage.SessionTitle)

nextCursor.description: NextCursor selects the next page (cursor parameter) when HasMore

Span.description: Span is a span (Duration in nanoseconds)

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the stored session of the span (read from storage;
ignored when spans are stored, which take it from SpanAttributes)

SpansResponse.description: SpansResponse is a page of the spans of a trace view, oldest first

nextCursor.description: NextCursor selects the next page (cursor parameter) when HasMore

total.description: Total counts all spans of the trace view

trace.description: Trace describes all spans of the trace view, not only this page's

StatsResponse.description:
StatsResponse counts the stored telemetry (GET /api/stats): all of it, or
that of a time range

errorRate.description: ErrorRate is the percentage of spans with an error status

services.description: Services lists all services that sent telemetry, whatever the range

growthBytesPerDay.description:
GrowthBytesPerDay is the used space divided by the days between the
oldest and newest record, 0 while they are less than a day apart

memoryLimit.description:
MemoryLimit and Threads are AI_OBSERVER_DB_MEMORY_LIMIT and
AI_OBSERVER_DB_THREADS, empty and 0 for DuckDB's defaults

sizeBytes.description:
SizeBytes is the size of the database file, WALSizeBytes that of its
write-ahead log (0 when there is none)

usedBytes.description:
UsedBytes and FreeBytes are the used and free blocks inside the file
(pragma_database_size). Deleted data frees blocks, which new data
reuses; the file only shrinks when compacted (ai-observer compact,
with the server stopped), which CompactRecommended suggests when a
large share of it is free.

StatusImport.description: StatusImport sums up the imported and watched session files of a tool

StatusPricing.description: StatusPricing describes a pricing file in use (pricing.Files)

file.description: File is the name of the file, such as claude.json

lastUpdated.description: LastUpdated is the lastUpdated of the built-in file

models.description: Models counts the models with prices, overrides included

override.description:
Override is the path of the file from AI_OBSERVER_PRICING_DIR merged
over the built-in one, with its lastUpdated

StatusResponse.description:
StatusResponse describes the running server for a status page (GET
/api/status). It names settings, never their secret values: whether a
token is required, not the token.

httpInspector.description:
HTTPInspector describes the HTTP capture proxy (enabled false when it
does not run); never credentials

mode.description:
Mode is what the server runs: "serve" (OTLP and API), "watch"
(session files and API, no OTLP) or "serve+watch" (OTLP, session files
and API: serve --watch)

watchedTools.description:
WatchedTools lists the tools whose session files are watched
(claude-code, codex, gemini) in watch and serve+watch mode

StatusServer.description: StatusServer describes where the server listens

otlpGrpcPort.description:
OTLPGRPCPort is the configured OTLP/gRPC port (AI_OBSERVER_OTLP_GRPC_PORT),
0 when it is turned off; OTLPGRPCEnabled reports whether it listens
(false in watch mode)

otlpPort.description:
OTLPPort is the configured OTLP port; OTLPEnabled is false in watch
mode, which does not listen on it

StatusSettings.description:
StatusSettings are the settings that change what is stored and who may
read it

adminApiEnabled.description:
AdminAPIEnabled is AI_OBSERVER_ADMIN_API; BackupDir is where the
admin API writes backups and exports (only set when it is enabled)

allowedHosts.description:
AllowedHosts are the further host names the API accepts
(AI_OBSERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS; "*" for any)

authEnabled.description: AuthEnabled reports whether AI_OBSERVER_AUTH_TOKEN is set

corsOrigin.description:
CORSOrigin is the browser origin the API answers CORS requests of
(AI_OBSERVER_FRONTEND_URL)

logFormat.description: LogFormat is AI_OBSERVER_LOG_FORMAT in effect: text or json

logLevel.description: LogLevel is AI_OBSERVER_LOG_LEVEL in effect: DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR

maxDbSizeBytes.description:
MaxDBSizeBytes is AI_OBSERVER_MAX_DB_SIZE, 0 for no limit: the oldest
days are deleted while the used blocks exceed it

redaction.description: Redaction is AI_OBSERVER_REDACT: secrets, all or off

retentionDays.description: RetentionDays is AI_OBSERVER_RETENTION_DAYS, 0 to keep everything

tlsEnabled.description:
TLSEnabled reports whether the servers speak TLS
(AI_OBSERVER_TLS_CERT and AI_OBSERVER_TLS_KEY); the files are not named

StatusTelemetry.description:
StatusTelemetry counts the stored telemetry (the cached /api/stats) and
gives the time of its oldest and newest record

StoredNotification.description:
Notification is the payload of a message: it tells clients that new records
were stored, without their content. Clients re-query the API for the data,
so prompts, code and tool output are not pushed to every open browser, and
large ingestion batches do not turn into large WebSocket frames.

TimeSeries.description:
TimeSeries is a series of [timestamp (Unix ms), value] points; the
timestamp is 0 for the single point of an aggregate. A value is NaN, sent
as JSON null, where a bucket has no value: histogram statistics other than
sum and count, and gauges, in buckets without points.

TimeSeriesResponse.description: TimeSeriesResponse holds the series of a metric (GET /api/metrics/series)

interval.description:
Interval is the bucket size in seconds: the requested one, or a
coarser one when the range would have too many buckets; 0 for
aggregates

metricType.description:
MetricType is the type of the points read (sum, gauge, histogram,
exponential_histogram, summary); empty without points in the range

stat.description:
Stat is the statistic of histogram series (MetricQuery.Stat, avg when
the query named none)

timeZone.description: TimeZone is the IANA zone the buckets are aligned to

TraceGroupLevel.description:
Levels of Codex traces (TraceOverview.GroupLevel)
- codex_turn: A trace of a Codex turn (root turn/start)
- codex_operation: A Codex operation (TraceKindCodexOperation)

TraceKind.description:
Kinds of trace views (TraceOverview.Kind, the kind parameter of GET
/api/traces/{id})
- otel_trace: An OpenTelemetry trace: the spans with one trace ID
- codex_operation: The spans of one operation of an older Codex session trace: a first-level span and its descendants (detail views only)

TraceOverview.description:
TraceOverview describes a trace (or a Codex operation) for lists and
detail views: its root span and all of its spans

duration.description:
Duration from the start of the earliest span to the end of the
latest, in nanoseconds

id.description:
ID identifies the trace view: the trace ID, or the root span ID of a
Codex operation

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the session of the trace's spans, when those that have
one have the same (their SessionId: the first of tools.SessionIDKeys)

startTime.description: StartTime is the start of the earliest span

TraceStatus.description:
Statuses of traces (TraceOverview.Status, storage.TraceStatus)
- ERROR: A span failed
- OK: No span failed and one succeeded
- UNSET: No span has a status

TracesResponse.description: TracesResponse is a page of traces, the most recent first

nextCursor.description: NextCursor selects the next page (cursor parameter) when HasMore

total.description:
Total counts the traces matching the query, HasMore whether pages
follow this one

TranscriptMessage.description: TranscriptMessage is a message of a transcript

index.description:
Index is the message's number in its source (not its position in
the transcript)

success.description: Tool execution success (pointer to distinguish false from unset)

TranscriptResponse.description:
TranscriptResponse contains the transcript of a session, or a page of its
messages (transcript.Page): Total counts all messages of the session, and
NextCursor requests the messages after this page when HasMore

messages.description: Messages are a page of the session's messages, oldest first

nextCursor.description: NextCursor selects the next page (cursor parameter) when HasMore

search.description: Search lists the matching messages (only with the search parameter)

title.description: Title is the first user prompt of the transcript (see Session.Title)

total.description: Total counts all messages of the session

totals.description: Totals sum all messages of the transcript, not only this page's

TranscriptSearch.description:
TranscriptSearch lists the messages of a whole transcript that contain all
search terms

matches.description:
Matches are the positions (0-based, ascending) of the matching
messages among all messages of the transcript: position p is on the
page that starts at the multiple of the page size below p

terms.description:
Terms are the words and "quoted phrases" read from the search
parameter

TranscriptTotals.description: TranscriptTotals are the totals of all messages of a transcript

toolCalls.description:
ToolCalls counts the tool_use messages, ToolErrors the tool_result
messages with success false

UpdateDashboardRequest.description:
UpdateDashboardRequest changes the name and description of a dashboard
(those it sets)

UpdateHTTPCaptureRunRequest.description:
UpdateHTTPCaptureRunRequest renames a run or sets its note; omitted
fields stay

UpdateWidgetPositionsRequest.description: UpdateWidgetPositionsRequest moves widgets of a dashboard

UpdateWidgetRequest.description:
UpdateWidgetRequest changes the fields of a widget that it sets: a
non-empty title, positions and spans above 0, and the config when present
(it replaces the stored config whole; {} clears it)

WebSocketMessage.description: WebSocketMessage is a message of the real-time WebSocket (GET /ws): one JSON text frame each

WebSocketMessageType.description:
What a real-time message announces: stored spans, metric points, log records or HTTP capture exchanges
- http_exchanges: MessageTypeHTTPExchanges announces HTTP capture exchanges stored or updated (service "http-proxy")

WidgetConfig.description: WidgetConfig holds optional configuration for configurable widgets

breakdownAttribute.description:
BreakdownAttribute is the attribute key series are broken down by
(such as type or model)

breakdownValue.description:
BreakdownValue is the value of BreakdownAttribute a metric value
widget shows

chartStacked.description: ChartStacked stacks a chart's bars (default true)

stat.description: Stat is the statistic of a histogram metric (MetricQuery.Stat)

WidgetPosition.description: WidgetPosition moves a widget to a grid cell

WireAPIError.description:
APIError is an error object of the API: {"type":"error","error":{...}}
as a JSON body or as an SSE error event

WireCacheBreakpoint.description: CacheBreakpoint is a cache_control marker in a request

ttl.description: TTL is cache_control.ttl ("5m", "1h"), empty when not given

WireCertainty.description:
Certainty of an observation: what the wire showed, or a conclusion drawn
from it

WireContentBlock.description:
ContentBlock is a content block of a message, as received or
reconstructed from content_block_* events

id.description:
ID, Name, Input of tool_use, server_tool_use and mcp_tool_use blocks.
In a stream Input is set only when the concatenated input_json_delta
fragments (PartialInput) form valid JSON; InputError says why not.

raw.description:
Raw is the block as received (content_block_start's block, or the
block of a JSON message), with fields this type does not know

stopped.description:
Stopped is set when content_block_stop was received (streams), or for
blocks of a complete JSON message

thinking.description:
Thinking and Signature of thinking blocks; Data of redacted_thinking
blocks (opaque, never interpreted)

toolUseId.description: ToolUseID of result blocks such as web_search_tool_result

WireDecodeStatus.description:
Body decoding status (DecodeBody)
- identity: no content coding: the bytes as they are
- decoded: decoded from the listed codings
- unsupported: a coding this package cannot decode
- error: corrupt data
- truncated: decoded output exceeded the limit

WireFieldChange.description:
FieldChange is a request parameter that differs between two requests
(JSON values; empty when absent)

WireMessage.description:
Message is a reply of POST /v1/messages: parsed from a JSON body, or
reconstructed from its SSE events

complete.description:
Complete: a JSON message was parsed whole, or a stream reached
message_stop with every started block stopped. An interrupted stream
is never complete, even when it has content.

error.description: Error is an error object (JSON error body, or SSE error event)

eventCounts.description: EventCounts counts the stream's events by type

extra.description: Extra holds top-level fields this type does not know

notes.description: Notes are parse problems (invalid JSON, unexpected order, ...)

streamed.description: Streamed tells whether the message came from SSE events

usageSnapshots.description:
UsageSnapshots are the usage objects of a stream in order (cumulative:
the last one is the reference, they are never added up)

WireMessagesSummary.description: MessagesSummary describes the messages array of a request

hashes.description:
Hashes are the SHA-256 (hex, first 16 characters) of each message's
JSON bytes as sent without its cache_control members, in order, for
prefix comparison (DiffRequests): clients move the cache breakpoint
to the newest message, which must not make older messages differ

roles.description:
Roles counts messages by role; Blocks counts content blocks by type
(a string content counts as one "text" block)

sizes.description: Sizes are the JSON bytes of each message

WireObservation.description:
Observation is one evidence-based statement about an exchange, for the
didactic view. Text is Brazilian Portuguese; it states what the wire
showed, never what the model "thought" or what the client did locally.

code.description:
Code is a stable identifier: assistant_text, tool_use,
assistant_thinking_available, server_tool_event, stop_reason,
api_error, tool_result_submitted, context_change, cache_breakpoint,
tool_definitions_provided, token_count, other_api, transport_error,
stream_partial, possible_compaction, unknown

evidence.description:
Evidence names the fields the statement is based on, such as
"response.content[1].type=tool_use"

WireParseStatus.description:
Parse status of a stream event's data (StreamEvent.ParseStatus)
- empty: no data
- truncated: data cut by the parser's limit
- mismatch: event: field differs from the JSON "type"

WireRequestDiff.description:
RequestDiff compares a request with an earlier one (DiffRequests). It
works on the summaries' fingerprints, never on the bodies, so its cost
does not grow with the size of the conversation.

commonPrefix.description: CommonPrefix is the number of leading messages with equal hashes

messagesAdded.description:
MessagesAdded are the messages after the common prefix in the later
request; MessagesReplaced the earlier request's messages after it
(history rewritten, e.g. by compaction)

newBytes.description:
NewBytes are the JSON bytes of the added messages, RepeatedBytes those
of the common prefix (history sent again)

newToolResults.description:
NewToolResults are tool_use IDs of tool_result blocks that the earlier
request did not carry

possibleCompaction.description:
PossibleCompaction: the history was rewritten (common prefix shorter
than the earlier request) and the message count dropped. A hint, not
a certainty.

WireRequestSummary.description:
RequestSummary is what ParseRequest reads from a Messages API request
body (also count_tokens requests, which share the shape)

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the session_id in metadata.user_id (a JSON string with
"session_id", or the legacy "..._session_<id>" form); empty otherwise

thinking.description: Raw JSON of fields shown as they are

toolUses.description: ToolUses are the tool_use blocks in the request's history

unknownFields.description:
UnknownFields are the top-level keys not in KnownRequestFields, in
order of appearance

valid.description: Valid is false when the body is not a JSON object; ParseError says why

WireSystemSummary.description: SystemSummary describes the system field of a request

bytes.description: Bytes of the system field's JSON, SHA256 of those bytes (hex)

WireToolDef.description: ToolDef is one entry of a request's tools array

type.description: Type is set for server/versioned tools (e.g. web_search_20250305)

WireToolResultRef.description: ToolResultRef is a tool_result block of a request

contentBytes.description: ContentBytes is the size of the block's content JSON

preview.description:
Preview is the start of the result's text (at most 300 bytes, cut at
a UTF-8 boundary); callers sanitize it before storing

WireToolUseRef.description: ToolUseRef is a tool_use block found in a request's history or a reply

WireToolsSummary.description: ToolsSummary describes the tools array of a request

WireUsage.description:
Usage is a usage object of the Messages API, normalized. A nil field was
not reported: never treat it as 0.

cacheCreation5m.description:
CacheCreation5m and CacheCreation1h are usage.cache_creation.
ephemeral_5m_input_tokens / ephemeral_1h_input_tokens: parts of
CacheCreationInputTokens, never added to it again

raw.description:
Raw is the usage object as received (for a stream, the last one
observed, see Message.UsageSnapshots)

WireUsageSnapshot.description: UsageSnapshot is a usage object observed in a stream, in order

eventSeq.description: EventSeq is the SSE event the usage came from

eventType.description:
EventType is message_start or message_delta (or another type that
carried usage)

usage.description: Usage is the cumulative usage after this event (merged snapshot)

WireUsageTotals.description:
UsageTotals are the totals derived from a Usage by the documented rules:

	total_input     = input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens
	total_processed = total_input + output_tokens
	cache_read_share = cache_read_input_tokens / total_input (total_input > 0)

A total is nil when its first term (input_tokens, resp. total_input and
output_tokens) is nil; absent cache fields are not counted, and Complete
tells whether all three input fields were reported.

cacheWriteUnknown.description:
CacheWriteUnknown is cache_creation_input_tokens minus the 5m and 1h
parts, when all three are known and it is above 0: cache writes whose
duration the API did not report. When neither part was reported it
is all of cache_creation_input_tokens (if above 0).
